title: Quantitative Formula Quick Reference
tagline: Year 4 — The formulas that cover most aptitude questions, each with a one-line use and a worked check

introduction.overview: This is a revision sheet in text form. Each entry gives the formula, when to use it and a small worked check so that you can verify that you remember it correctly. The set covers percentages, profit and loss, ratio, averages, interest, time and work, time and distance, mixtures, permutations and combinations, and geometry. The best use of a quick reference is to cover the right-hand side and reproduce it from memory.
introduction.placementRelevance: The night before a test, a formula sheet you have already practised is the most efficient revision.
introduction.realWorldContext: Reference sheets and checklists support accurate work in any technical job.

learningObjectives: Recall the core formulas from memory
Apply each with a one-line check
Choose the right formula for a question
Test yourself by covering the answers

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Revision means retrieval: try to produce the formula before reading it.

coreDefinitions: Formula: a rule expressing a relation.
Check: a small example that confirms the formula.
Retrieval practice: recalling instead of rereading.
Similar formulas: ones that are easy to confuse.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A formula is a compressed story; the check restores the story.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Cover the formula, recall it, then uncover and compare.

mainNarrative: Percent change: from 80 to 100 the change is 20; 20 ÷ 80 = 25%.
Compound amount: ₹10,000 at 10% for 2 years is 10,000 × 1.21 = ₹12,100.
Average speed over equal distances at 60 and 40 km/h is 2 × 60 × 40 ÷ 100 = 48 km/h.
Two workers taking 12 and 24 days finish together in 8 days.
